The Healthcare Data Landscape {background-color="#01364C"} ## Four Sources, Four Lenses {.smaller} | | **Claims** | **EHR** | **Public / Census** | **Vendor** | |---|---|---|---|---| | **What** | Bills sent to an insurer | Clinical record of care | ACS, CDC SVI, PLACES | Purchased SDOH, consumer, benchmark data | | **Grain** | One row per service line | One row per encounter / lab / vital | One row per ZIP, tract, county | One row per person (if matched) | | **Owner** | Payers (Highmark, Medicaid) | Providers (Epic, Cerner) | Government | Data companies | | **Strength** | Complete *billed* picture across all providers, with **cost** | Clinical detail: labs, vitals, PHQ-9 | Free, broad context | Fills social gaps | | **Gotcha** | No results, codes ≠ truth, reversals | Only *in-network* care, messy entry | Area ≠ person (ecological) | Match rates, black-box methods | ## How They Link {.big-mermaid} ```{mermaid} %%| echo: false %%| fig-width: 10 flowchart LR M["members

Hands-On: Juniper Health Plan {background-color="#01364C"} ## Meet the Data {.smaller} *Juniper Health Plan* is **fictitious** — 3,000 Utah members in 2025. ::: {#af4591a2 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} claims = pd.read_csv("data/claims.csv", parse_dates=["service_date"]) members = pd.read_csv("data/members.csv", parse_dates=["enroll_start", "enroll_end"]) ehr = pd.read_csv("data/ehr_encounters.csv", parse_dates=["encounter_date"]) xwalk = pd.read_csv("data/mrn_crosswalk.csv") census = pd.read_csv("data/census_zip.csv", dtype={"zip": str}) vendor = pd.read_csv("data/vendor_sdoh.csv") members["zip"] = members["zip"].astype(str) members["age"] = 2025 - members["birth_year"] pd.Series({k: len(v) for k, v in dict(claims=claims, members=members, ehr=ehr, xwalk=xwalk, census=census, vendor=vendor).items()}, name="rows") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` claims 27948 members 3000 ehr 4783 xwalk 1857 census 12 vendor 2494 Name: rows, dtype: int64 ``` ::: ::: # Claims {background-color="#02577B"} ## What a Claim Looks Like {.smaller} ::: {#db4ad20f .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} claims.sample(6, random_state=3)[["member_id", "service_date", "place_of_service", "dx1", "procedure_or_drug", "paid_amt"]].reset_index(drop=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
member_id service_date place_of_service dx1 procedure_or_drug paid_amt
0 M100754 2025-12-24 11 Office E66.01 99213 151.11
1 M100997 2025-02-26 Pharmacy NaN GLP-1 RA 660.51
2 M101877 2025-04-23 11 Office E11.9 99214 110.34
3 M101270 2025-04-26 02 Telehealth R51.9 99213 126.94
4 M101523 2025-07-31 11 Office M54.50 99213 137.19

``` ::: ::: - `dx1` = ICD-10 diagnosis · `procedure_or_drug` = CPT code or drug class - `place_of_service` tells you *where*: office, ED (23), inpatient (21), telehealth (02) ## Gotcha: Reversals {.smaller} Claims get reversed and resubmitted. Sum dollars **by claim** before anything else. ::: {#2e72019f .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} claims["claim_status"].value_counts() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` claim_status paid 27535 reversed 413 Name: count, dtype: int64 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#7aff3a20 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} net = (claims.groupby(["claim_id", "member_id", "service_date", "claim_type", "place_of_service", "dx1", "procedure_or_drug"], dropna=False) [["allowed_amt", "paid_amt"]].sum().reset_index()) net = net[net["paid_amt"] > 0] # fully reversed claims drop out len(claims), len(net) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` (27948, 27122) ``` ::: ::: ## PMPM: The Payer's Favorite Metric {.smaller} **P**er **M**ember **P**er **M**onth = total paid ÷ member-months ::::{.columns} :::{.column width="52%"} ::: {#ffb934b4 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} paid = net.groupby("member_id")["paid_amt"].sum() mem = members.assign( paid=members["member_id"].map(paid).fillna(0)) pmpm = (mem.groupby("plan_type") [["paid", "member_months"]].sum()) pmpm["pmpm"] = pmpm["paid"] / pmpm["member_months"] pmpm["pmpm"].round(0) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` plan_type Commercial 151.0 Medicaid 183.0 Medicare Advantage 313.0 Name: pmpm, dtype: float64 ``` ::: ::: ::: :::{.column width="48%"} ::: {#93a22aa3 .cell execution_count=7} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ![](healthcare_analytics_files/figure-revealjs/cell-8-output-1.png){width=750 height=660} ::: ::: ::: :::: Why divide by member-months? Not everyone is enrolled all year. ## Cost Is Concentrated The top **5%** of members account for **43%** of spend; the top 20% for **76%**. ::: {#885dc83d .cell execution_count=9} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=9} ![](healthcare_analytics_files/figure-revealjs/cell-10-output-1.png){width=1125 height=630} ::: ::: This is why care management programs target "high utilizers." ## Where Does the Money Go? {.smaller} ::::{.columns} :::{.column width="50%"} ::: {#cb8497ad .cell execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} by_pos = (net.groupby("place_of_service") ["paid_amt"].agg(["sum", "size"])) by_pos["share_of_$"] = by_pos["sum"] / by_pos["sum"].sum() by_pos["share_of_claims"] = by_pos["size"] / by_pos["size"].sum() by_pos[["share_of_claims", "share_of_$"]].round(2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=10} ```{=html}
share_of_claims share_of_$
place_of_service

11 Office 0.32 0.17
21 Inpatient Hospital 0.00 0.34
23 Emergency Room 0.03 0.22
Pharmacy 0.57 0.23
``` ::: ::: ::: :::{.column width="50%"} ::: {#b0aa3fbb .cell execution_count=11} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=11} ![](healthcare_analytics_files/figure-revealjs/cell-12-output-1.png){width=780 height=660} ::: ::: ::: :::: Inpatient: few claims, big dollars. Pharmacy: most claims, dollars driven by a few drugs. ## Your Turn: Claims {.smaller background-color="#F7F8F9"} :::{.callout-tip} ## 5 minutes 1. Which **diagnosis codes** (`dx1`) show up most in ED visits (`place_of_service == "23 Emergency Room"`)? 2. What share of pharmacy dollars goes to **GLP-1 RA**? How many members fill one? ::: ::: {.fragment} ::: {#e906f00b .cell execution_count=12} ``` {.python .cell-code} ed = net[net["place_of_service"].str.startswith("23")] print(ed["dx1"].value_counts().head(3)) rx = net[net["claim_type"] == "pharmacy"] print(rx.groupby("procedure_or_drug")["paid_amt"].sum().div(rx["paid_amt"].sum()).round(2).sort_values().tail(3)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` dx1 R07.9 156 J06.9 153 R55 145 Name: count, dtype: int64 procedure_or_drug ACE inhibitor 0.04 inhaled corticosteroid 0.06 GLP-1 RA 0.86 Name: paid_amt, dtype: float64 ``` ::: ::: ::: # Electronic Health Records {background-color="#02577B"} ## Linking EHR to Claims EHRs use a **medical record number (MRN)**, not a member ID. We need a crosswalk. ::: {#21f3c0c0 .cell execution_count=13} ``` {.python .cell-code} ehr_m = ehr.merge(xwalk, on="mrn", how="left") cov = members["member_id"].isin(ehr_m["member_id"]).mean() print(f"{cov:.0%} of members have any EHR data") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 62% of members have any EHR data ``` ::: ::: The rest got care **outside** this health system: the EHR only sees in-network care. ## Gotcha: Data Entry Errors ::: {#8662ef08 .cell execution_count=14} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=14} ![](healthcare_analytics_files/figure-revealjs/cell-15-output-1.png){width=1125 height=630} ::: ::: ::: {#176eeebe .cell execution_count=15} ``` {.python .cell-code} ehr_m.loc[~ehr_m["bmi"].between(12, 70), "bmi"] = np.nan # set impossible values to missing ``` ::: ## Who Has Diabetes? Depends Who You Ask {.smaller} ::::{.columns} :::{.column width="55%"} ::: {#e92b2ff3 .cell execution_count=16} ``` {.python .cell-code} dx = set(net.loc[net["dx1"] == "E11.9", "member_id"]) rx = set(net.loc[net["procedure_or_drug"] == "metformin", "member_id"]) lab = set(ehr_m.loc[ehr_m["a1c"] >= 6.5, "member_id"]) def found_by(m): hits = [n for n, ids in [("Dx", dx), ("Rx", rx), ("Lab", lab)] if m in ids] return " + ".join(hits) or "none" linked = ehr_m["member_id"].dropna().unique() combo = (pd.Series([found_by(m) for m in linked]) .value_counts().drop("none")) ``` ::: ::: :::{.column width="45%"} ::: {#dc3257c2 .cell execution_count=17} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=17} ![](healthcare_analytics_files/figure-revealjs/cell-18-output-1.png){width=690 height=660} ::: ::: ::: :::: Any single source **misses people**. Combining claims (Dx, Rx) with EHR labs gives a fuller picture. (We did this for depression at Highmark; see Part 4.) ## Your Turn: EHR {.smaller background-color="#F7F8F9"} :::{.callout-tip} ## 5 minutes Use each linked member's **highest PHQ-9** to assign depression severity (0–4 none/minimal, 5–9 mild, 10–14 moderate, 15–19 mod-severe, 20+ severe). How many with a PHQ-9 ≥ 10 have **no** depression diagnosis (`F32*`/`F33*`) in claims? ::: ::: {.fragment} ::: {#be4c76f7 .cell execution_count=18} ``` {.python .cell-code} phq = ehr_m.groupby("member_id")["phq9"].max().dropna() sev = pd.cut(phq, [-1, 4, 9, 14, 19, 27], labels=["none", "mild", "moderate", "mod-severe", "severe"]) dep_dx = set(net.loc[net["dx1"].str.match(r"F3[23]", na=False), "member_id"]) high = phq[phq >= 10].index print(sev.value_counts().sort_index().to_dict()) print(f"PHQ-9 ≥ 10 without a dx: {(~high.isin(dep_dx)).sum()} of {len(high)}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` {'none': 706, 'mild': 290, 'moderate': 83, 'mod-severe': 31, 'severe': 20} PHQ-9 ≥ 10 without a dx: 46 of 134 ``` ::: ::: ::: # Public / Census Data {background-color="#02577B"} ## Adding Neighborhood Context {.smaller} The **Social Vulnerability Index (SVI)** ranks areas 0–1 on poverty, housing, transportation, etc. ::: {#420f6bac .cell execution_count=19} ``` {.python .cell-code} census.head(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=19} ```{=html}
zip county svi median_hh_income pct_poverty pct_uninsured pct_age65plus population
0 84321 Cache 0.42 71600 13.1 8.7 20.6 31990
1 84341 Cache 0.22 90800 8.7 7.5 12.5 40696
2 84302 Box Elder 0.55 57000 16.3 8.9 17.7 10767
``` ::: ::: ::: {#a1f946fe .cell execution_count=20} ``` {.python .cell-code} ed_n = ed.groupby("member_id").size().rename("ed_visits") by_zip = (mem.merge(ed_n, on="member_id", how="left").fillna({"ed_visits": 0}) .groupby("zip")[["ed_visits", "member_months"]].sum() .merge(census, on="zip")) by_zip["ed_per_1000"] = 12_000 * by_zip["ed_visits"] / by_zip["member_months"] ``` ::: ## ED Visits Rise with Vulnerability ::: {#595be6f7 .cell execution_count=21} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=21} ![](healthcare_analytics_files/figure-revealjs/cell-22-output-1.png){width=1125 height=630} ::: ::: ⚠️ **Ecological fallacy:** a ZIP's SVI describes the *area*, not the person. # Vendor Data {background-color="#02577B"} ## Buying What You Can't Observe {.smaller} Vendors link consumer records to members and sell **person-level** social risk. ::::{.columns} :::{.column width="50%"} ::: {#b9ed133c .cell execution_count=22} ``` {.python .cell-code} v = members[["member_id"]].merge( vendor, on="member_id", how="left") conf = v["match_confidence"] print(f"Matched: {conf.notna().mean():.0%}") print(f"High-confidence: {(conf >= .7).mean():.0%}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Matched: 83% High-confidence: 67% ``` ::: ::: ::: :::{.column width="50%"} ::: {#3167675c .cell execution_count=23} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=23} ![](healthcare_analytics_files/figure-revealjs/cell-24-output-1.png){width=750 height=570} ::: ::: ::: :::: Ask every vendor: *how* did you match, *how* is this score built, and *who* is missing? ## Food Insecurity and the ED {.smaller} ::::{.columns} :::{.column width="52%"} ::: {#0b70e866 .cell execution_count=24} ``` {.python .cell-code} dat = (mem.merge(ed_n, on="member_id", how="left") .fillna({"ed_visits": 0}) .merge(census, on="zip") .merge(vendor, on="member_id") .query("match_confidence >= 0.7")) dat["fi_q"] = pd.qcut(dat["food_insecurity_index"], 4, labels=["Q1 low", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4 high"]) q = (dat.groupby("fi_q", observed=True) [["ed_visits", "member_months"]].sum()) q["per_1000"] = 12_000 * q["ed_visits"] / q["member_months"] q["per_1000"].round(0) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=24} ``` fi_q Q1 low 219.0 Q2 279.0 Q3 367.0 Q4 high 438.0 Name: per_1000, dtype: float64 ``` ::: ::: ::: :::{.column width="48%"} ::: {#4c3ea8f3 .cell execution_count=25} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=25} ![](healthcare_analytics_files/figure-revealjs/cell-26-output-1.png){width=750 height=660} ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Putting It All Together: A Poisson Model {.smaller} ED visits are counts with unequal exposure, so use Poisson with an **offset** for member-months. ::: {#65ec02bb .cell execution_count=26} ``` {.python .cell-code} dat["diabetes_dx"] = dat["member_id"].isin(dx).astype(int) fit = smf.glm("ed_visits ~ food_insecurity_index + svi + age + diabetes_dx + C(plan_type)", data=dat, family=sm.families.Poisson(), offset=np.log(dat["member_months"])).fit() ``` ::: ::: {#57da188c .cell execution_count=27} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=27} ![](healthcare_analytics_files/figure-revealjs/cell-28-output-1.png){width=1125 height=540} ::: ::: ## Your Turn: Vendor + Model {.smaller background-color="#F7F8F9"} :::{.callout-tip} ## 5 minutes 1. Add `housing_instability` and `transportation_barrier` to the model. Do they matter after food insecurity? 2. Refit using **all** matched members (no confidence filter). Does the food-insecurity IRR change? ::: ::: {.fragment} ::: {#b67f2d8c .cell execution_count=28} ``` {.python .cell-code} fit2 = smf.glm("ed_visits ~ food_insecurity_index + housing_instability + transportation_barrier" " + svi + age + diabetes_dx + C(plan_type)", data=dat, family=sm.families.Poisson(), offset=np.log(dat["member_months"])).fit() np.exp(fit2.params).round(2) ``` ::: ::: # 3. Careers in Healthcare Analytics {background-color="#01364C"} ## The Field Is Growing ::: {#18203478 .cell execution_count=29} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=28} ![](healthcare_analytics_files/figure-revealjs/cell-30-output-1.png){width=1275 height=645} ::: ::: ~**25,000** data scientist openings per year, and **insurance carriers** are among the top employers of data scientists (10%). ## Where the Jobs Are {.smaller} ::::{.columns} :::{.column width="50%"} **Payers (insurers)** : Claims, cost of care, risk adjustment, HEDIS / Star ratings **Providers (health systems)** : EHR reporting, quality, operations, readmissions **Pharma & life sciences** : Real-world evidence, outcomes research ::: :::{.column width="50%"} **Health tech & data vendors** : Products built on claims / SDOH data **Consulting** : Value-based care, program evaluation **Government & public health** : Medicaid, state health departments, CDC ::: :::: :::{.callout-note} **In Utah:** Intermountain Health / Select Health, University of Utah Health, Optum, HealthEquity, Regence BCBS, Utah DHHS ::: ## What Postings Ask For {.smaller} *Composites of typical 2026 postings, not a specific employer.* ::::{.columns} :::{.column width="33%"} **Healthcare Data Analyst**
*Health system* - Build dashboards on quality & throughput - Pull from **Epic Clarity/Caboodle** - Track readmissions, LOS, no-shows - **SQL**, Tableau / Power BI - BS + 1–3 yrs ::: :::{.column width="33%"} **Claims / Payer Analyst**
*Insurer* - PMPM, utilization, trend reporting - **ICD-10, CPT, NDC**, HEDIS, risk scores - Program ROI for care management - **SQL**, Python/R, Excel - BS + 2–4 yrs ::: :::{.column width="33%"} **Health Data Scientist**
*Payer, provider, or vendor* - Predictive models (risk, readmission) - **Causal inference**: matching, DiD - Partner with clinicians & executives - **Python/R**, SQL, cloud - MS preferred ::: :::: ::: {.fragment} **Common thread:** SQL + a language + healthcare data fluency + **explaining results to non-analysts.** ::: # 4. Real Work: Highmark Health {background-color="#01364C"} ## Manager of Advanced Analytics Highmark is a **payor-provider** system: an insurer (Highmark) *and* a health network (Allegheny Health Network). That means claims **and** EHR on the same people. ::: {#b448c1f1 .cell execution_count=30} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=29} ![](healthcare_analytics_files/figure-revealjs/cell-31-output-1.png){width=1275 height=660} ::: ::: "Derived / vendor": multi-source scoring frameworks and predicted race used where data were missing. ## GLP-1s vs Bariatric Surgery {.smaller} ::::{.columns} :::{.column width="60%"} ![](images/highmark_glp1_weight.png) ::: :::{.column width="40%"} **Data:** Highmark claims + AHN EHR (weights) **Design:** 30,458 patients with class II/III obesity; propensity-score weighting; mixed-effects models for monthly cost **Findings (2 yrs):** - Weight loss: **28.3%** surgery vs **10.3%** GLP-1 - Total cost: **$51,794** surgery vs **$63,483** GLP-1 - Driver: ongoing pharmacy spend Barrett et al. (2025). *JAMA Surgery*, 160(11), 1232–1239. ::: :::: ## Depression: Finding It and Costing It {.smaller} ::::{.columns} :::{.column width="50%"} ![](images/highmark_depression_cost.png) ::: :::{.column width="50%"} **Identify & stratify** with claims + EHR (Dx, Rx, PHQ-9, utilization) - Found **720,882** members with depression - **258,206 more** than diagnosis codes alone **Cost of severity change** (PMPM, 2019 → 2020) - Severity ↑ : **+$608** PMPM on average - Severity ↓ : **−$41** PMPM Popkov, Barrett, et al. (2026). *J Behav Health Serv Res*; Popkov, Barrett, et al. (2025). *J Affect Disord*, 368, 41–47. ::: :::: Same idea as our diabetes Dx/Rx/Lab exercise, at scale. ## Palliative Care: Payor-Provider Partnership ::: {#28911627 .cell execution_count=31} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=30} ![](healthcare_analytics_files/figure-revealjs/cell-32-output-1.png){width=1200 height=570} ::: ::: **$4.5M** total savings · hospice use **84% vs 50%** · Jaffe, …, Barrett (2025). *J Palliat Med*. ## More from the Same Toolkit {.smaller} | Question | Data | Method | Finding | |---|---|---|---| | Is adolescent depression screening equitable? | Claims + **SVI** | Multilevel logistic | Higher SVI → lower screening odds; pediatricians OR = 9.6 | | What does insomnia cost? | Claims, ~3M members | Propensity matching, GLMs | 9% have insomnia, **21%** of total spend | | Does measurement-based care reduce ED use? | Claims + registry | Negative binomial, survival | **34% lower** ED visit rate (IRR = 0.66) | Galper et al. (2025) *AJPH*; Karlin et al. (2024) *Sleep Adv*; Breitzig et al. (2026) *Adm Policy Ment Health*. ::: {.fragment} Every one started as a **business question** from a clinical or finance partner. ::: ## Takeaways 1. **Claims** = cost & breadth · **EHR** = clinical depth · **Census** = context · **Vendor** = gaps filled (at a price) 2. Most of the work is **linking and cleaning**: reversals, crosswalks, implausible values, match rates 3. No single source finds everyone. **Combine them.** 4. The field is **growing**, and it rewards people who can *explain* results to clinicians and executives :::{.callout} **Keep playing:** all data is in `data/` and `data/make_data.py` regenerates it. ::: ## Sources {.smaller} - U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, *Occupational Outlook Handbook*: [Data Scientists](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/math/data-scientists.htm), [Medical & Health Services Managers](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/medical-and-health-services-managers.htm), [Health Information Technologists](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/health-information-technologists-and-medical-registrars.htm), [Operations Research Analysts](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/math/operations-research-analysts.htm), [Mathematicians & Statisticians](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/math/mathematicians-and-statisticians.htm) - Barrett TS, et al.
